results.title: Ghanaian engineer Johannes Amo-Aye wins Africa Prize award for hybrid wind and solar innovation
results.content: Ghanaian engineer Johannes Amo-Aye has won the £5,000 One-to-Watch Award at the 2026 Africa Prize for Engineering Innovation for developing a hybrid wind and solar energy system designed to provide reliable electricity to off-grid communities. His innovation, the Fusion Wind Turbine, combines wind and solar power to provide electricity to underserved communities, particularly rural health facilities that rely on expensive diesel generators during power outages. The award, decided by an audience vote, was presented at a ceremony held at NH Johannesburg Sandton in South Africa. Amo-Aye's recognition comes as the continent continues to grapple with electricity access challenges, with more than 600 million people in sub-Saharan Africa living without reliable electricity. results.title: Former convicts recount broken marriages, family rejection after prison as Crime Check Foundation calls for change
results.content: Former prisoners have shared painful accounts of broken marriages, abandoned families and rejection by loved ones following their release from prison, highlighting the difficulties many face in rebuilding their lives after serving their sentences.

results.title: Farmers fight Lands Commission, Newmont for delayed compensation over Ahafo North Mines Project
results.content: The Concerned Farmers Association of Afrispakrom, Terchire, Susuanso, and Adrobaa in the Tano North Municipality of the Ahafo region has called on the Land Valuation Division of the Lands Commission to immediately pay all outstanding compensation for lands, crops, and farm structures acquired for Newmont Ghana Gold Ltd’s Ahafo North mining project.

results.title: SEND Ghana warns unhealthy diets could raise a generation of diabetics, calls for mandatory food labels
results.content: SEND Ghana has warned that the growing consumption of ultra-processed foods among children could increase the country's future burden of diabetes, hypertension and other non-communicable diseases (NCDs).

results.title: Daily Insight for CEOs: Executive accountability for results
results.content: Organizational performance improves when executive leaders take clear ownership of results. Accountability must go beyond attending meetings, submitting reports, and completing assigned activities. It requires executives to accept responsibility for outcomes, explain performance gaps, and take corrective action.

results.content: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has commended President John Dramani Mahama for his leadership in driving reforms in Ghana and contributing to efforts to address pressing global challenges.

results.title: NAIMOS, Navy immobilise illegal mining equipment on River Offin amid armed resistance
results.content: The National Anti-Illegal Mining Operations Secretariat (NAIMOS), supported by personnel from the Ghana Navy Special Boat Squadron, has returned to the River Offin in the Central Region, immobilising equipment allegedly used for illegal mining and polluting the waterbody. The operation took place at Nipanekro in the Upper Denkyira West District, following an earlier attempt by NAIMOS to stop illegal mining activities along the river that was reportedly met with stiff resistance from Changfan operators. In a report by JoyNews' Erastus Asare Donkor, the Navy personnel deployed an inflatable boat to cross the river and reach the opposite bank, where the mining equipment was located.

results.title: AMA gives traders at unauthorised bus stops 48 hours to vacate
results.content: The Accra Metropolitan Assembly (AMA) has given traders occupying unauthorised bus stops across the metropolis 48 hours to cease trading and vacate the locations ahead of an enforcement exercise. In a statement issued on Wednesday, November 4, 2026, the Assembly said the directive followed concerns raised by commercial drivers over the obstruction of designated bus stops by hawkers and other traders. The AMA said the practice obstructed the movement of vehicles and pedestrians, contributed to traffic congestion and forced commuters to board and alight from vehicles at unsafe locations, increasing the risk of road accidents. results.content: The Minister for Lands and Natural Resources, Emmanuel Armah-Kofi Buah, has outlined major reforms in the new Mining Act currently before Parliament, which he says will transform mining communities, stop licence speculation and significantly increase Ghana's mineral revenues.

results.title: Ejisu to celebrate maiden Yaa Asantewaa I festival to rebuild burnt museum
results.content: The Ejisu Traditional Area is set to celebrate the maiden Nana Yaa Asantewaa I festival from December 24 to 27 2026, in honour of the legacy of the brave female warrior of the Asante kingdom.

results.title: GPRTU, GRTCC call off planned sit-down strike after meeting with ministers
results.content: The Ghana Private Road Transport Union (GPRTU) and the Ghana Road Transport Coordinating Council (GRTCC) have called off their planned sit-down strike following assurances from government to address concerns over trading activities on road corridors. The two transport groups announced the planned sit-down strike on November 2, 2026, protesting what they described as the authorities' failure to clear roadways of trading activities. The proposed action was expected to disrupt commercial transport services across the country. The latest decision means transport services will continue without the disruption that would have resulted from the planned strike. results.title: Government explores light rail network on four major Accra routes – Mahama Ayariga
results.content: The government is considering replacing the Aayalolo bus contra-flow system with a light rail network as part of efforts to develop a more permanent solution to Accra's growing transportation challenges.

results.title: NPP’s GH¢5,000 parliamentary application fee could sideline women, youth – GenCED
results.content: The Gender Centre for Empowering Development (GenCED) has warned that the reported GH¢5,000 parliamentary candidate application fee introduced by the New Patriotic Party (NPP) could deepen financial barriers to political participation, particularly for women, young people and persons with disabilities. The NPP recently announced a GH¢5,000 application fee for parliamentary aspirants, alongside a GH¢2,000 fee for declaring interest. The party has defended the charges as necessary to ensure that only serious candidates proceed to the nomination stage. In a statement issued on Friday, October 30, 2026, the organisation said although political parties had legitimate administrative and organisational costs, their candidate selection requirements should not unnecessarily disadvantage qualified individuals from groups historically underrepresented in political leadership.

results.title: Kasoa to get new air quality monitors as EPA moves to close Central Region’s data gap
results.content: Air pollution kills tens of thousands of Ghanaians every year, yet in much of the country no one is measuring it. The State of Global Air 2025 report found that air pollution claimed over 32,000 lives in Ghana in 2023, nearly 14% of all deaths, making it the country’s second leading risk factor for death, behind high blood pressure. It is linked to 39% of stroke deaths, 66% of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease deaths, and a third of neonatal deaths. The damage builds up over a lifetime. The Air Quality Life Index found that Ghana’s average PM2.5 level in 2023 stood at 12.91 micrograms per cubic metre, more than double the World Health Organisation’s guideline of 5. At that level, polluted air cuts nearly a year from the average Ghanaian life. The problem is that air pollution is mostly invisible. results.title: Traffictech: We’ve written to road sector agencies to fix all road markings – NRSA

results.title: Why Fix the Problem when we can Go on Strike?
results.content: Ghana has finally found a formula to solve all problems: When something offends you, go on strike. Commercial drivers have announced a nationwide strike today, November 4, because of TRAFFITECH-GH. Their argument is simple and touching. Traders have occupied the bus stops and pedestrian walkways, so they cannot park properly. And since they cannot park properly, they should not be fined by cameras for speeding, running red lights, not wearing seatbelts, or driving with expired licences, insurance and roadworthiness. Let us applaud the logic.

results.title: Students to study in Ghana and abroad under proposed higher education policy
results.content: The government says it is prioritising transnational education to expand access to higher education and meet growing demand from Ghana's youth population. Under the policy, joint and double-degree programmes will become compulsory, allowing students to complete portions of their academic programmes in Ghana and at partner institutions abroad. Speaking at the Study in Europe Fair 2026, Education Minister Haruna Iddrisu said the initiative would give students international academic exposure while helping them maintain a strong connection to Ghanaian institutions.
